findings.problem: The Risks bullet rightly says the cut "is not a sandbox", but it leaves "the rest" to this review, and the plan that held the detail (section 4.4, which also understates it as "close the two easy ways out (docker, sudo)") is deleted before ready. The rest: code inside the cut keeps the runner's uid and shares the filesystem and process table with what runs after it, so it can get code run outside the cut. Exploit sketch: a compromised dev dependency (vitest, vite, or the rolldown and lightningcss native binaries, all of which run inside the cut) writes `core.fsmonitor = <script>` into the workspace's .git/config. After the cut, actions/checkout's post-job step runs `git submodule foreach --recursive ...` outside the cut, and git runs the script there with the network, the docker group and passwordless sudo.
findings.evidence: toolchain.yml:68-73 (setpriv keeps uid 1001; no mount or PID namespace). CI log, PR job 131510257155, lines 447-463: checkout's post step runs `/usr/bin/git submodule foreach --recursive ...` after the cut. Local test in a fresh scratch repository: a hook planted in `core.fsmonitor`, then `git submodule status` (the same submodule-listing code path; the guard refused the exact `foreach` here) ran the hook (marker lines with args 2 and 1). git-config(1): core.fsmonitor holds "the pathname of the \"fsmonitor\" hook command". network_namespaces(7) isolates only "the UNIX domain abstract socket namespace", so pathname sockets stay reachable: the D-Bus system bus, and systemd-resolved's socket if the image has it, through which name lookups leave the machine (from documentation, untested on the runner). Code inside can also signal the runner's own processes, which run as the same user. Impact: contents: read and no secrets today. Possible reach into main-scope caches, including the Playwright cache that the required smoke check restores, rests on recall (JavaScript actions carry the cache token). gate.yml's toolkit dependencies have the same exposure today.

findings.problem: setpriv drops privileges without `--inh-caps=-all` (setpriv(1)'s own advice when dropping from root) and without `--bounding-set=-all`. The cut prints `id` and `ip -o link` but asserts none of its properties. Today the result is right, but it relies on sudo's root having empty inheritable and ambient sets, and on the step shell not being root. Exploit sketch: none on today's runner. If the step shell ran as root (a container job, or a self-hosted runner), `--reuid="$(id -u)"` becomes 0, so the code inside the cut keeps root and full capabilities (and could re-enter the host network namespace) while every step stays green.
findings.evidence: toolchain.yml:69-74; the CI log prints `uid=1001(runner) gid=65534(nogroup)` and only `lo` (PR job 131510257155 :254-255), printed but never checked. setpriv(1): "Setting a uid or gid does not change capabilities, although the exec call at the end might change capabilities. This means that, if you are root, you probably want to do something like: setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --inh-caps=-all". Local test, util-linux 2.39.3 as root: with the job's flags, CapInh/CapPrm/CapEff/CapAmb 0, CapBnd = the parent's 000001fffeffffff, NoNewPrivs 1; with `--inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all` added, the same but CapBnd 0000000000000000, exit 0. The full bounding set is inert today: under no_new_privs "the set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits as well as file capabilities will be disabled" (setpriv(1)).
findings.fix: At 2.3 (a CI edit, so it asks Mustafa): add `--inh-caps=-all --bounding-set=-all` to the setpriv call. Inside the cut, before the tests, fail unless `id -u` is not 0, `ip -o link` lists only `lo`, and `/proc/self/status` shows CapInh, CapPrm, CapEff, CapAmb and CapBnd all zero and NoNewPrivs 1. Those crates have overflow checks off in release, so there the checks vanish and the code wraps silently. Two statements therefore do not hold in the release server or the release Wasm: the comment on line 21 ('Overflow checks in every profile for the simulation and the protocol') and ADR part 4's 'a debug client and a release server never disagree on overflow'. This is not OVERFLOW-WASM, which treats native release as proven; native release has the same hole. Nor is it OVERFLOW-PER-CRATE, which covers crates that hold sim arithmetic; this is sim's own code compiled into crates that hold none, so that remedy does not close it. Reach is zero today.
